hook: The giant tsar who dragged Russia into the modern world.

pages.x: Peter was born in Moscow in 1672 and became tsar at ten, sharing the throne with his half-brother. As a boy he saw palace guards murder his relatives in a revolt. Kept away from the Kremlin, he played war games with real cannon and an army of hundreds of boys.

In 1697 he toured western Europe disguised as "Sergeant Pyotr Mikhailov", though at over two metres tall he was hard to miss. He worked as a carpenter in Dutch and English shipyards, learned to pull teeth, and peered through Leeuwenhoek's microscopes.
pages.img: Grand Embassy of Peter the Great

pages.x: Back home he cut off his nobles' beards with his own hands, and later taxed anyone who kept one; they had to carry a token to show they had paid. He made his courtiers wear Western clothes.
He built a modern army and Russia's first navy, and fought Sweden for 21 years for a coast on the Baltic Sea. In 1709 he crushed King Charles XII at Poltava, ending Sweden's days as a great power.
In 1703 he founded a new city on marshes at the mouth of the Neva, Russia's "window on Europe". Tens of thousands of forced labourers died building it. It was the capital of Russia for 200 years.
His son and heir Alexei opposed his reforms and fled abroad. Peter lured him home and had him tortured, and Alexei died in prison in 1718.
In 1724 he waded into freezing water to help rescue soldiers from a boat that had run aground. He fell ill, and died a few months later, in 1725.
Peter forced Russia into the modern world, with a navy, a new capital, schools and Western ways. He made Russia a great European power, at a terrible cost in lives.
pts: Made Russia a great European power
